figure_caption: Reporting after search. A benchmark sample of $N$ questions is used to search $K$ configurations; the search log and the selected configuration are passed to a post-hoc reporter, which returns a point estimate and a 90% interval for the selected configuration's accuracy on fresh questions. We compare the naive Wilson interval, a Bonferroni-widened interval, a question-resampling optimism correction, and the EB-IRT posterior interval, all scored against known truth by an evaluator that owns the worlds, searchers and truth.

panels.title: Reporting after search: problem and compared reporters
panels.short_caption: Search log and selected configuration feed four post-hoc reporters, scored against known fresh-question accuracy.
panels.drawio_prompt:
Single idea: a benchmark sample is searched over K configurations, and the search log plus the selected configuration are handed to four post-hoc reporters whose 90% intervals an evaluator scores against known fresh-question accuracy. One connected left-to-right flow on a wide (21:9) canvas.

NODES (stable IDs, semantic encoding):
- worlds (sharp box, data source, small, top-left): label "Worlds". Two tiny sub-lines: "Synthetic" and "Real: Qwen2.5-0.5B / MMLU-Pro".
- sample (sharp box, data): "Benchmark sample" with symbol $$N$$ questions.
- search (rounded box, process): "Search over $$K$$ configs". Beneath it two small tag chips: "Exhaustive" and "Successive halving".
- log (sharp box, data, document-like): "Search log" with sub-label "(question, config, outcome)".
- khat (sharp small box, data): "Selected config $$\hat{k}$$".
- Reporter group (a large labeled container, dashed outline, title "Post-hoc reporters"; the search is never touched, so no edge returns into search). Inside it four stacked rounded boxes, same size, top to bottom:
  - rep_naive: "Naive Wilson"
  - rep_bonf: "Bonferroni-Wilson"
  - rep_resamp: "Question resampling"
  - rep_ebirt: "EB-IRT posterior" with a small "ours" tag. This is the most important node; it is the only one that is a fitted (trainable/estimated) model, so give it a distinct sub-label "Hierarchical latent difficulty".
- out (sharp box, data): ONE shared box "Estimate + 90% interval" with symbols $$\hat{\theta}, [\ell, u]$$ that all four reporters feed.
- Evaluator group (large labeled container at right, dashed outline, title "Evaluator"): contains
  - truth (sharp box, result/ground truth): "Fresh-question accuracy $$\theta_{\hat{k}}$$" with sub-label "known truth".
  - score (rounded box, process): "Interval score" with small symbol $$\mathrm{IS}_{0.10}$$, plus sub-chips "Coverage" and "Width".
  Worlds, search and truth each carry the same small corner tag "evaluator-owned" (the evaluator owns the worlds, searchers and truth); worlds and search sit outside the Evaluator container.

EDGES (source -> target, solid = forward data flow, dashed = auxiliary / evaluation only):
1. worlds -> sample, solid, no label.
2. sample -> search, solid, label "$$N$$ questions" (or no label if crowded).
3. search -> log, solid, no label.
4. search -> khat, solid, no label.
5. log -> each of rep_naive, rep_bonf, rep_resamp, rep_ebirt, solid. Draw as one fan-out trunk splitting into four branches (the trunk enters the Reporter container, branches reach each box).
6. khat -> Reporter container, solid, merges into the same trunk (or enters the container separately); label none.
7. each reporter -> out, solid, four short edges converging on out.
8. out -> score, solid, label "scored".
9. truth -> score, dashed (evaluation only), label "compare".

SPATIAL LAYOUT: five columns left to right: (1) worlds above/over sample, stacked vertically; (2) search with log and khat stacked below/beside it, log above khat; (3) Reporter container with the four reporters stacked vertically and vertically centred on the canvas; (4) out box, centred; (5) Evaluator container with truth above score, vertically centred. Keep rep_ebirt visually first among equals (e.g. bottom-most or aligned on the main horizontal axis) so the eye lands on it. Keep all four reporter boxes equal size and evenly spaced. Align columns on a common horizontal centreline; avoid edge crossings except the unavoidable fan-out.

IMPORTANCE RANKING: (1) rep_ebirt, (2) the four-reporter comparison group as a whole, (3) log + khat -> reporters hand-off, (4) out and score/truth, (5) worlds, sample, search.

TEXT BUDGET (exact labels, names only, no sentences): "Worlds"; "Synthetic"; "Real: Qwen2.5-0.5B / MMLU-Pro"; "Benchmark sample"; "$$N$$ questions"; "Search over $$K$$ configs"; "Exhaustive"; "Successive halving"; "Search log"; "(question, config, outcome)"; "Selected config $$\hat{k}$$"; "Post-hoc reporters"; "Naive Wilson"; "Bonferroni-Wilson"; "Question resampling"; "EB-IRT posterior"; "Hierarchical latent difficulty"; "ours"; "Estimate + 90% interval"; "$$\hat{\theta}, [\ell, u]$$"; "scored"; "Evaluator"; "Fresh-question accuracy $$\theta_{\hat{k}}$$"; "known truth"; "compare"; "Interval score"; "$$\mathrm{IS}_{0.10}$$"; "Coverage"; "Width"; "evaluator-owned". No raw multi-term equations anywhere; no deferred plots or placeholders are needed.
